analysis.investment_thesis: QPOWER has decent capital returns (ROCE 26.6%) but trades at an earnings yield of ~0.7% (EBIT ₹65 Cr / EV ₹9,168 Cr), catastrophically failing the Magic Formula's core cheapness test. A good business at 87x earnings is not a good investment.
key_strengths: High ROCE of 26.6% and operating margin of 19%+ — capital-light for an equipment business
Revenue CAGR of 22.6% with operating profit CAGR of 41.4% (2022–2025) — genuine growth
Near-zero leverage (D/E 0.05, net cash ₹172 Cr) — fortress balance sheet
key_risks: Earnings yield ~0.71% (EBIT ₹65 Cr / EV ₹9,168 Cr) — Magic Formula requires >12%; this fails by a factor of 17x
Other income ₹54 Cr vs operating income ₹65 Cr — nearly half of profits are non-operating, inflating apparent quality
Post-IPO equity surge (₹153 Cr → ₹469 Cr equity, financing CF ₹171 Cr in 2025) — valuation bakes in perfection with fresh capital still undeployed
red_flags: Other income (₹54 Cr) is 54% of net profit (₹100 Cr) — operating earnings are far weaker than headline numbers suggest
Investing CF of -₹100 Cr in 2025 against OCF of ₹62 Cr — heavy reinvestment, FCF only ₹39 Cr vs ₹100 Cr net profit
EV/EBITDA of 59x and P/S of 12x — the market has already priced in many years of flawless execution
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on QPOWER produces a clear verdict. Earnings Yield = EBIT (₹65 Cr) / EV (Market Cap ₹9,340 + Debt ₹9 - Cash ₹181 = ₹9,168 Cr) = **0.71%** — a number so far below my 12% threshold it doesn't even warrant a ranking. Return on Capital is acceptable at 26.6% ROCE, but the Magic Formula requires BOTH legs of the equation to work. One leg (cheapness) is broken beyond repair at this price. Even generous assumptions — using EBITDA of ₹115 Cr instead of EBIT — yield only 1.25%.

The quality-of-earnings picture raises further concerns. Other income of ₹54 Cr in FY25 accounts for 54% of net profit of ₹100 Cr. Strip that out and core operating profit is just ₹65 Cr against a ₹9,340 Cr market cap — a pure-play P/E closer to 145x. The FY25 balance sheet explosion (assets ₹359 Cr → ₹978 Cr, equity ₹153 Cr → ₹469 Cr) is consistent with a recent IPO raising ~₹171 Cr; the fresh capital sits largely idle in cash while the market assigns a 19.9x price-to-book on it. The business itself — serving renewable energy, railways, and power utilities with specialized power electronics — is genuinely well-positioned. But the Magic Formula is a price-disciplined system: a great business at a terrible price is simply a bad investment.
